key_insight: A graph neural network can learn systematic energy offsets between different DFT workflows and translate heterogeneous formation energies onto a common, higher-accuracy scale.
engineering_relevance: This enables legacy and multi-source DFT datasets to be merged reliably, improving downstream materials design tasks such as phase stability, battery voltages, and reaction thermodynamics.
method: Use 380,190 paired PBE–r2SCAN structures from MatPES.
Train a structure-aware GNN to predict cross-functional energy residuals.
Convert PBE energies to r2SCAN-level estimates via transfer learning with GPTFF architecture.
evidence_signal: The model reaches 14.3 meV/atom MAE for PBE-to-r2SCAN conversion, improving over CHGNet at 18.2 meV/atom; the abstract notes an average 107 meV/atom discrepancy between PBE and r2SCAN for identical structures.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability and quality of paired cross-functional reference data, and extrapolation to unseen functionals or chemistry should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Aligning Heterogeneous DFT Datasets: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Cross-Functional Formation Energies
